name: Basilica of the National Shrine of Our Lady of San Juan del Valle
history: A priest in the Rio Grande Valley commissioned a Guadalajara artist to copy the statue of the Virgin of San Juan de los Lagos, and a shrine was built here in 1954. On 23 October 1970 a low-flying plane crashed into the shrine, which burned; only the tower survived. A priest and the sacristan saved the statue. The new shrine was dedicated on 19 April 1980 before about 50,000 people and named a basilica in 1999.
arch: A large modern shrine church. The surviving tower of the old shrine still stands to the south.
features: Thirty life-size bronze Stations of the Cross line a three-quarter-mile path.
The exterior mural "Jesus Presents His Mother" was blessed in 1995.

look.d: This tower is all that survived the 1970 plane crash and fire.
Saturdays and Sundays bring the most pilgrims.

fun: The statue is a copy of the Virgin of San Juan de los Lagos in Jalisco, Mexico.
journal: A shrine that burned and rose again, with the old tower standing guard.

quiz.q: Where was the statue's model venerated?
a: San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico
